name: Claims Lodgement Officer vehicle guided flow full conversation
simulation_scenario: A claimant phones CGU to lodge a vehicle claim. They are cooperative and answer clearly and truthfully whenever Amanda asks a question, but they do NOT volunteer any information before it is asked for — they wait for each question and answer only that question, one field at a time (this is a guided-flow conversation, not an express/upfront dump). When asked what happened, they say they were rear-ended at a red light. When asked for the date and time, they say the 3rd of March at around 2pm. When asked for the vehicle registration, they say ABC-123. When asked for the incident location, they say the corner of Smith and King Street. When asked for a policy number, they say POL-123456. When asked for a contact method, they give the email john.smith@example.com. When asked for their name, they say John Smith. If Amanda guesses the spelling of their name and asks them to confirm, or asks them to spell it, they confirm J-O-H-N S-M-I-T-H is correct. If asked whether they have another claim to lodge, they say no. They answer every question on the first attempt without hesitation or ambiguity, and never repeat information they've already given unless Amanda explicitly asks them to repeat it.
success_condition: Judge the ENTIRE conversation from Amanda's opening greeting through to the end of the call. PASS requires ALL of the following: (1) Amanda never asks the claimant for the same field twice — she does not re-ask for anything already stated earlier in the conversation (not policy number, not what happened, not date/time, not registration, not incident location, not contact method, not first name, not last name, not name-spelling confirmation once it has been confirmed once). (2) Amanda collects every required vehicle-claim field before closing: claim type, policy number, what happened, date and time of incident, vehicle registration, incident location, contact method, first name, last name, and an explicit claimant confirmation of the name spelling (agent guessing the spelling and the claimant confirming it counts). (3) Amanda asks for fields one at a time (guided flow), not all at once. (4) The conversation reaches a valid close within the turn budget: Amanda delivers a closing line equivalent to 'I've recorded your details. Our team will be in touch within two business days.' and then calls end_call — she must NOT say the claim has been 'lodged', must NOT mention a claim number, and must NOT promise an email confirmation. (5) Amanda does not call end_call while a required field, including name-spelling confirmation, is still missing. FAIL if any field is re-asked after already being collected, if any required field (including name-spelling confirmation) is skipped before closing/end_call, if the conversation does not reach the closing line and end_call within the turn budget, or if the closing line implies a claim number, lodgement confirmation, or email follow-up.
